Automatically loaded project instructions (PROJECT.md):
# Pocket Notes

A mobile-first notes app. Its two screens are a draft editor and a saved-notes list.


## Conventions
Use the existing storage module for persistence. Preserve the DOM data-testid attributes because browser tests use them. Keep user text as text, not interpreted HTML. Preserve existing notes and the current appearance. No dependencies are needed.

## Verification
Use run_checks for actual browser acceptance checks. Inspect the returned failures, then rerun after editing. The protected checks are outside this repository. A passing result belongs only to the source revision it tested.

## Completion
A draft survives navigation and page refresh. Saving creates exactly one note, clears the draft, and preserves other notes. Distinct notes stay distinct. Explain the change and its verification in the final summary.

events.detail:
All 6 acceptance checks pass on the current revision. The fix is complete.

## Summary

**Problem:** Drafts were never persisted. `src/storage.js` had `readDraft()` always returning `{ title: '', body: '' }`, while `writeDraft()` and `clearDraft()` were empty stubs. So typing in the editor, switching to "My notes", or refreshing the page lost the draft, and save had nothing real to clear.

**Change (`src/storage.js` only):** Implemented draft persistence using the same `localStorage` prefix module convention already used for notes:
- `readDraft()` reads the stored draft, falling back to an empty draft.
- `writeDraft(draft)` persists the draft to `localStorage` (called on every input in `src/app.js`, which was already wired up).
- `clearDraft()` removes the stored draft (called after save).

No changes to `src/app.js` or `src/styles.css` — the draft input handlers and save flow were already correct; they just had no storage backing. Appearance, `data-testid` attributes, seed notes, escaping of user text, and unique `crypto.randomUUID()` note IDs (keeping distinct notes distinct) are all unchanged.

**Verification:** `run_checks` against the current revision passed all 6 browser acceptance criteria: draft survives switching screens, draft survives page refresh, save persists exactly one note, saving clears the draft, existing notes are preserved, and distinct notes remain distinct.
